title: Adherence support for a community falls prevention exercise programme: a pragmatic trial in 14 centres
abstract: Objective: to test whether reminders, missed-week calls, peer volunteer calls and a home exercise calendar increase attendance at a 24-week community strength and balance programme. Design: pragmatic trial with individual allocation stratified by centre. Primary outcome: attendance at 32 or more of 48 sessions. Results will follow the trial.
introduction: Community strength and balance programmes prevent falls only if people keep attending. A recorded search found one trial of reminders and one comparison of peer calls; other suggested studies were unverified leads.
methods: Central allocation after consent, usual classes and instructors, register-based attendance, phone checks for home exercise, monthly falls calendars, intention-to-treat analysis.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present recruitment, delivery of the package, attendance by arm with the risk difference, secondary outcomes and falls.
discussion: The discussion will consider contamination within classes, who the package reached, and why falls were not powered.
limitations: Unblinded; contamination; self-reported home exercise and falls.
conclusion: To be written after the trial.
reportingChecklist: CONSORT extension for pragmatic trials with TIDieR
summary: CONSORT-structured draft with results left empty.
